To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the preserved ability in aged AO rats to produce both proinflammatory TN-α and antiinflammatory IL-10 cytokines most likely contributes to the longer average life span of AO rats compared with DA rats.
the age-related changes in macrophage functions are strain specific, and that the preserved ability to synthesize IL-10 in macrophages from AO rats may contribute to their longer average longevity.
aging differentially affects the surface expression of macrophage TLR4 and co-receptor CD14, the production of cytokines TNF-α or IL-10 and the activity of iN0S or arginase in DA and AO macrophages.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new aspect of the aging process, i.e., the strain-specific changes of macrophage functions with aging.
the age-related changes in macrophage functions, which are important for understanding the age-dependent changes in the immune responses and may have implications in aging-related disorders.
the age-related changes in functional characteristics of macrohages from different rat models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
aging in AO rats, contrary to DA rats, is not associated with a shift towards the Th1 immune response, which is typical for the aged immune system.
the strain specificity of age-dependent changes in the functional characteristics of peritoneal macrohages is associated with their ability to produce TNF-α as well as IL-10.
aging in DA rats results in a decrease of the ability of peritoneal macro phages to synthesize TNF-α.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
macrophages from AO rats are better equipped to maintain their functions during aging, and thus contribute to a more efficient immune response in elderly AO rats.
the aging-related changes in macrophage functions in rats depend on both genetic background and the strain-specific aging process.
macrophages from the long-lived rats are characterized by the ability to produce both pro-inflammatory and regulatory cytokines, which is a feature of macrophages in healthy young animals.
The main takeaway from our work is that

aging affects the phenotypic characteristics of macrophage surface receptors in a strain-specific manner, which in turn determines the ability of macrophage to synthesize pro- and anti-inflammatory mediators, thereby contributing to the strain-specific longevity.

macrophages from rats of different strains differ in their ability to synthesize IL-10 with aging, which is associated with the strain-specific changes in the surface expression of macrophage TLR4 and co-receptor CD14.
aging affects the phenotypic characteristics of macrophage differently in rats of different strains.
